provenance.notes: Pilot file. Board family is clean with the rfq archetype override, so the buyer is a facilities or office manager. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Square footage, floor types, restroom count, cleaning frequency, after-hours access and alarm procedure, and a calendar for the site walkthrough
pageStructurePlus.why: Every commercial cleaning bid starts with a walkthrough. A buyer who can book one online skips the phone tag that loses the bid.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Nightly, weekly and monthly task lists by area: restrooms, break rooms, offices, lobbies, trash and recycling, high dusting
pageStructurePlus.why: Facilities managers compare janitorial bids line by line. Showing the scope up front makes the bid easy to approve.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Strip and wax for VCT, carpet extraction, tile and grout, burnishing schedules, and which floors get what and how often
pageStructurePlus.why: Floor care is the line that separates one cleaning bid from another and the one buyers ask about after a bad winter.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The supervisor inspection checklist, how a tenant reports a missed task, how fast it gets fixed, and how keys and alarm codes are handled
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers switch cleaning vendors over missed tasks that nobody followed up. A visible reporting loop answers the reason they're shopping.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The product approach, safety data sheets on request, who stocks paper and soap, and green cleaning options for tenants who ask
pageStructurePlus.why: Office managers get asked about chemicals and empty dispensers. Answering both on the page removes two follow-up emails.

designDirections.name: Clean Bid
designDirections.bestFor: Owner-led crews bidding on small offices and medical suites near home
designDirections.headlineSample: Office cleaning in {City}, done every night
designDirections.whyItFits: Evergreen reads as clean without the spa feel, and the serif headings give a small cleaning company the steadiness an office manager wants to see.

designDirections.name: Facility Ready
designDirections.bestFor: Janitorial companies bidding multi-site contracts that live or die on a capability page
designDirections.headlineSample: Commercial janitorial for {City} offices and facilities
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Fresh Fern, fails CTA contrast and leans residential. Cobalt Wire's neutral sans and blue accent read as procurement-ready.

designDirections.name: Night Shift
designDirections.bestFor: Established firms selling inspection reports and accountability to property managers
designDirections.headlineSample: Nightly janitorial for {City} buildings, inspected and reported
designDirections.whyItFits: A dark, mono-labelled page matches work done after hours and makes inspection data and response times feel like the product.

openers.line: Your Google listing has a phone number but no website, so an office manager asked to find three janitorial bids in {City} has nothing to forward to their boss.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a facilities manager would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing goes to a Facebook page about house cleaning specials. A building manager looking for a commercial cleaning contract reads that as the wrong company.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and note where it lands and whether it mixes residential and commercial cleaning.
openers.linkLine: A page built for the commercial cleaning buyer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with an old phone number and no service list. Procurement checks the janitorial vendor's site before the walkthrough, and that one raises questions.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old number, a dead form, a builder banner. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Same janitorial company, current and complete: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your site on my phone and the cleaning services list wouldn't scroll. Facility managers do vendor research between meetings on their phones.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same cleaning company, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to request a walkthrough for office cleaning except calling during the day, which is when your crews are asleep. A form with square footage and frequency would catch those bids.
openers.hook: Check the listing and any site for a quote or walkthrough form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A walkthrough request that asks the right questions: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your strip-and-wax and carpet extraction posts show real floor care, and they're buried on Facebook. A capability page with that floor work would win the bids that ask about floors.
openers.hook: Find one floor care or before-and-after post on their pages. Name the floor type if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your floor care work on a capability page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You have Google reviews from office managers saying the cleaning crew is reliable. A facilities buyer would want those next to the bid, not on a map listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase from a business customer. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your commercial reviews next to the scope of work: {demo-link}

openers.line: A lot of office cleaning contracts come up for renewal with the budget year. The janitorial companies a manager can find that month are the ones on the shortlist.
openers.hook: Use this in the two months before the fiscal year turns for local offices, schools or government buildings. Name the month.

openers.line: Your crews clean offices at night and the buyers call at ten in the morning. If that call goes to voicemail, the bid goes to a cleaning company that picked up.
openers.hook: Call their listed number mid-morning. If it goes to voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A janitorial page that takes the bid request while you sleep: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring night cleaners. Good applicants check whether a janitorial company looks steady before they apply, and so do the buildings you bid on.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note, a job board listing or a sign. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A cleaning company page with a hiring section in two languages: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing says you clean offices across {City}, but there's no page showing which business parks and suburbs you cover. Facilities buyers search by area.
openers.hook: Find the areas they mention in posts or reviews and use the one furthest from their base.
openers.linkLine: A coverage page for your commercial cleaning routes: {demo-link}

openers.line: Commercial cleaning buyers ask about net-thirty terms and invoicing before they ask about price. If that's answered on your site, the office manager can approve you without a call.
openers.hook: Only if they already invoice businesses. Check reviews or posts for commercial clients first.
openers.linkLine: Janitorial terms answered before the bid: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every building manager asks a janitorial vendor for a certificate of insurance before the walkthrough. A page that says you're insured, bonded and background-checked answers it early.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured and bonded' on their listing or posts. Never claim coverage you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance, bonding and background checks on one cleaning page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your office cleaning contracts come from one manager telling another. That works until a building changes hands and the new manager searches instead.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or posts that mention a property manager or a referral. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred building manager would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is real janitorial work. A job like that belongs on a capability page a facilities manager can forward.
openers.hook: Pick their newest commercial job post and name it: the building type and the work done.
openers.linkLine: That commercial cleaning job on a capability page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is real janitorial work.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the Facebook page but nothing a facilities manager could forward. I put together a sample capability page with a walkthrough request and a sample scope of work, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample commercial cleaning site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a walkthrough request, a nightly and weekly scope of work, and a page for insurance and bonding. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.

IF NO:

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a janitorial company your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}, less than a month on one office contract."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, late morning or early afternoon?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: All my contracts come from referrals.
objections.handler: "Then your cleaning is good. The referred manager still checks you before the walkthrough, and the site gives them something to forward to whoever signs the contract."

objections.objection: Buildings find us through bid sites, not websites.
objections.handler: "Bid portals bring the RFP. The capability page is what the evaluator opens next to your bid, with your scope, floor care and insurance in one place."
"That's why I built it first. I need about twenty minutes of your time, and I'll write the janitorial scope from your current contracts."
"You have a page for house cleaning. Commercial buyers want a walkthrough request, a scope of work and a certificate of insurance. That's a different site, or a different section."
"Perfect, I'll work with them directly. They give me the contract scopes and the insurance details, and they approve everything before it goes live."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a capability page, a walkthrough request and a coverage page. That's less than a month on one office cleaning contract."

{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} janitorial demo down on Friday to free up the space.

sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — office cleaning contracts in {City} start coming up for renewal with the new budget year. Thought of you.

The capability page is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one month of a mid-size office contract, never to the house-cleaning side of their business.
The capability page and the walkthrough request are the core. Price everything else as additions to those.
Price industry pages one at a time: medical offices, schools, warehouses and property managers each read a scope differently.
A downloadable capability statement is its own line; procurement teams attach it to the bid file.
Charge for a bilingual hiring section separately. Night-crew hiring is often the problem they feel first.
Keep the monthly add-ons small next to their contract values, so nobody questions them at renewal.

lineItems.description: Max with square footage, floor types, frequency, after-hours access questions and a calendar for the walkthrough.
Max when the page carries its own sample scope and the compliance notes that industry asks about.
Max when it includes the coverage map, insurance summary, floor care programme and references the client supplies.
Max with nightly, weekly and monthly task tables per area and a printable version.
Max when it covers several floor types with schedules and a before-and-after gallery from the client's own jobs.
Max with an applicant form in two languages, shift preferences and a route to the hiring manager's phone.
Max when each area page names the business parks served and the response time the client commits to.

whatElseYouSell.name: Bid packet and capability statement design
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every janitorial bid goes out with the same clean packet: capability statement, scope, insurance summary and references."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or before the next bid deadline they mention.

whatElseYouSell.name: Outreach to facilities and office managers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short monthly note to the office and property managers in your area, pointing at the capability page and a walkthrough slot."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the capability page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for commercial cleaning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "New commercial cleaning work on your Google profile every week, so it stops looking like a house-cleaning listing."

whatElseYouSell.name: Crew and floor care photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One evening shooting a crew in uniform and a floor job in progress gives the janitorial site real pictures instead of stock."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, at a client building that agrees in writing.

whatElseYouSell.name: Reference letter and review collection
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Happy office managers get a simple request for a review and a short reference letter for your next cleaning bid."

whatElseYouSell.name: Contract renewal campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before budget season, a short campaign to the buildings near your current cleaning routes, offering a walkthrough."
whatElseYouSell.when: Two months before the local fiscal year turns.

whatElseYouSell.name: Uniform, vehicle and site-sign artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Matching uniforms, a van decal and a small sign at the janitorial closet make the crew look like the company on the website."

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your cleaning supply distributor sells to every janitorial company in the region and has a catalog nobody can search. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have real budgets and their customer list is the prospect list you'd otherwise build by hand.

withoutAI.route: Window cleaning and pressure washing subs
withoutAI.whoPays: The sub, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who does the windows and the sidewalks at the office buildings you clean? I'll build their site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: They work the same buildings on different schedules and already trade referrals.

withoutAI.route: The property management firms they clean for
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The property manager who hired your cleaning crew has a tenant request page from years ago. I can fix that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the vendors who show up every night. A janitorial owner's introduction gets a meeting.

withoutAI.route: Carpet extraction and floor refinishing subs
withoutAI.whoPays: The sub, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "If you sub out deep carpet or floor refinishing on your office buildings, that company needs a site as much as you did."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Specialty floor subs depend on janitorial companies for work and listen when one recommends you.

withoutAI.route: Pest control and landscaping vendors in the same buildings
withoutAI.whoPays: Each vendor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pest and grounds vendors at your office buildings face the same facilities buyer. I build their sites on the same capability layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same buyer, same procurement questions, so the capability page carries over almost unchanged.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Brokers leasing office space need a move-in vendor page for new tenants. Your cleaning company belongs on it, and I can build the page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Brokers refer vendors to every new tenant and pay for pages that make a lease feel turnkey.

withAI.route: Reorder assistant for the supply distributor
withAI.pitchLine: "Janitorial companies tell the assistant which buildings they clean, and it drafts the monthly supply order from the distributor's catalog."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps cleaning companies ordering from one distributor, which is worth more than a discount.

withAI.pitchLine: "Tenant complaints about a missed office cleaning task get sorted and sent to the right vendor before the manager reads them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers spend mornings forwarding complaints. Cutting that is easy to justify.

withAI.route: Quote assistant for the window cleaning sub
withAI.pitchLine: "The window crew on your office buildings quotes from building photos. An assistant drafts the quote from the pane count and height."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built once for the cleaning client's world, sold through their trust.

withAI.route: Tenant request assistant for building owners
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants ask about after-hours office cleaning, extra trash pickups or a spill, and the assistant logs it and tells the janitorial crew."
withAI.whyItWorks: Owners want fewer tenant calls. The janitorial client is already the one fixing what gets reported.

withAI.route: Photo-based floor estimate for the refinishing sub
withAI.pitchLine: "Building managers upload floor photos and a rough size, and the floor sub gets a draft estimate for strip, wax or extraction."
withAI.whyItWorks: Floor subs lose time driving to small jobs. A draft estimate filters them first.

withAI.route: Applicant screener for night-crew staffing agencies
withAI.pitchLine: "The staffing agency that sends night cleaners to your office buildings screens applicants by shift, area and transport with the same assistant you use."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agencies place workers with many janitorial firms. The client's introduction carries weight.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for walkthrough requests
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A facilities manager calls at ten in the morning, gets a text within a minute asking for the building and square footage, and you call back with the walkthrough booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Cleaning bid calculator by square footage and frequency
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the square footage, floor types and how many nights a week, and the calculator drafts the monthly janitorial price from your own rates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their production rates by area type and their margin rules.

softwareAI.name: Inspection checklist app with room-by-room proof
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Supervisors walk the building, check off each office and restroom, and the cleaning report goes to the client by morning."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their inspection checklist and a supervisor willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Bid writer from walkthrough notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the walkthrough on the way to the car, and a draft janitorial bid with scope and price is waiting when you get home."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past bids and the bid calculator's rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supply restock alerts by building
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Crews mark low paper, soap and liners at each building, and the cleaning supply order builds itself."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the building list and their supply order habits.

softwareAI.name: Client portal for work orders and cleaning reports
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Office managers log a missed task, see when it was fixed and download last month's inspection reports without emailing you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the inspection app. Needs their client list and an agreed response time.

softwareAI.name: Daytime receptionist while the night crew sleeps
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers the commercial cleaning line during the day, takes the building details and books the walkthrough, so the morning calls stop going to voicemail."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar, coverage area and the questions they ask on every walkthrough call. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew scheduling and building key log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Who cleans which building tonight, who holds which key and alarm code, all in one place instead of the owner's head."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run several crews. Needs the building list, crew list and key policy.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual applicant screener for night cleaners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for night cleaning shifts answer your questions in their language, and you only call the ones who fit the routes and hours."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they're hiring. Needs their must-haves, pay range and shift list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Contract renewal reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two months before an office cleaning contract renews, you get a reminder with the account's inspection history ready to share."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs contract start and end dates for each building.

softwareAI.name: Check-in and check-out at each building
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Crews check in and out on their phones at each building, so you can show an office manager exactly when the cleaning happened."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the building list and crew phones.

softwareAI.name: Site instructions translated for the crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each building's cleaning instructions, alarm steps and special requests, translated for every crew member and kept current."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs written site instructions and review by a bilingual supervisor. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per building
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which office buildings actually make money once labour hours and cleaning supplies are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs crew hours and supply costs per building for a few months.

softwareAI.name: Reference request and review reply drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Replies to every review and a reference request for each happy office manager, drafted in your voice for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the reference collection. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Invoicing with net-terms follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Monthly janitorial invoices go out on the first, and a polite follow-up goes to accounts payable when net terms run out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their accounting system and client billing terms.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot for janitorial scope and frequency questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you clean medical offices' and 'can you do three nights a week' from your real services, then books the walkthrough."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their service list, coverage and scheduling rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Floor care schedule tracker per building
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every building's strip, wax and carpet extraction dates in one schedule, with the client reminded before the floor crew arrives."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the floor types and schedules for each building.

softwareAI.name: Crew knowledge base of building procedures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New cleaners ask the phone how this building handles the alarm or the server room, and get the owner's answer instead of a guess."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs written procedures and the owner's approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Safety data sheet library per building
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every cleaning product used at each building, with its safety sheet, ready when a tenant or an inspector asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their product list per building.

softwareAI.name: Complaint-to-work-order triage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Client emails about a missed office or restroom get turned into work orders for tonight's crew, with a confirmation sent when it's done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the client portal. Needs the crew schedule. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the inspection app for janitorial companies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a janitorial inspection app for one company. Every commercial cleaning firm has to prove the work got done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client taught you the inspection workflow and paid for it. The problem is the same in every market.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License the bid calculator to a janitorial supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every cleaning company on your books a bid calculator that also drafts the supply order from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It ties customers to one distributor's catalog, which beats a volume discount.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member janitorial company a capability page template and a walkthrough request as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew, and one deal reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each of your cleaning territories needs coverage pages and a walkthrough request that routes to the right owner. I build it once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract, many territories, one template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Vendor compliance portal for a property management firm
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every cleaning and maintenance vendor uploads insurance and inspection reports to one portal, across all your buildings."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Large firms chase certificates of insurance constantly. The janitorial client's workflow is the proof you understand it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label janitorial site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets commercial cleaning clients and builds from scratch. License my capability template with the walkthrough request built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Applicant pipeline for night-crew staffing agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Janitorial companies call you for night cleaners. A bilingual applicant pipeline fills those orders faster."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies earn on placements, and the janitorial client knows exactly what a good applicant looks like.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Tenant services page for office brokerages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every office tenant you place needs cleaning, movers and IT. A tenant services page with vetted vendors makes your leases easier to close."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokerages want leases to feel turnkey, and the janitorial client is the first vetted vendor.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same janitorial stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New cleaning clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one commercial cleaning company per area. Yours is set in {City}. The next metro is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the capability page proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your group sells cleaning, maintenance and grounds under one contract. One capability site per trade, one walkthrough request for all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups that bundle trades buy sites in sets and renew them together.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Cleaning cost estimator for property managers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Property managers estimate office cleaning by building size and frequency, and the sponsoring janitorial firm gets the walkthrough request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It uses only the sponsor's own rates, so it never claims market data, and it sends the sponsor qualified requests.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your inspection or scheduling tool and disappeared. I've shipped that workflow for another cleaning company."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded clients already decided to buy. They need someone with the janitorial workflow already built.

upsellLadder.line: "Those morning calls are facilities managers. The receptionist books the walkthrough while your janitorial crew sleeps."

upsellLadder.trigger: They pass several buildings under contract or a property manager asks for monthly reports.
upsellLadder.line: "Your property managers want reports. Give them a portal and the cleaning contract renews itself."

upsellLadder.trigger: Two months before the local budget year turns.
upsellLadder.line: "Renewal season is coming. Let's put your janitorial company in front of the buildings near your routes first."
